name: Pildash
overview: Pildash is a male biblical figure identified primarily as the son of Nahor. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture provides no additional details about his tribe or other distinguishing notes. His mention is brief and limited to his lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Pildash means 'steely' or 'spider,' reflecting its Hebrew roots. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it carries a meaning that may suggest strength or intricacy.
familyAndRelationships: Pildash is recorded as a son of Nahor, which places him in the broader family line connected to Abraham. He is also listed alongside Milcah as a child of Nahor, indicating sibling relationships. Other familial ties are not documented in Scripture beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Pildash's significance lies in his genealogical connection to Nahor, who is part of the patriarchal lineage central to the biblical narrative. While Pildash himself does not have a prominent role or recorded deeds, his mention helps establish the family context from which key biblical figures emerge. His presence in Genesis 22:22 situates him within the unfolding story of God's covenant people.
